hits.name: Anthropic
hits.hook: Anthropic has filed an S-1 registration statement with the SEC related to its proposed IPO. Read more: Legal disclaimer: A registration statement relating to these securities has been filed with the SEC but has not yet b
hits.draft_en:
Anthropic just filed to go public.

What that actually means:
• An S-1 is the document a company files with the SEC before an IPO. It's where the real revenue and spending numbers live.
• Reported ticker: ANT on Nasdaq.
• In the filing, Anthropic says it expects AI that rivals top human experts and works on its own for weeks to be widely available within a few years.

For the first time, we get to see what a frontier AI lab really earns and burns.

Which number are you checking first?
hits.video_tip: Vertical 25s explainer: open on a stamped 'S-1' document sliding onto a desk, then a Nasdaq-style ticker strip reading 'ANT', then three quick text cards (What is an S-1? / Ticker: ANT / 'expert-level AI within a few years'). End on the question card. First-2s hook text: 'Anthropic just filed to go public'.

hits.name: OpenAI
hits.hook: GPT-6.1 Terra: delivering fast and capable computer use at a lower price. GPT-6.1 Terra understands what’s on screen, takes action across apps, writes naturally, and is a more capable model for your whole workday with th
hits.draft_en:
OpenAI's newest model isn't trying to be the smartest. It's trying to be the cheapest one that can use your computer.

GPT-6.1 Terra in 3 numbers:
• $1 in / $5 out per million tokens
• OpenAI says ~9x lower cost per task than Claude Opus 5.5 at max effort
• Built for computer use: it reads the screen and acts across your apps

The race is shifting from 'best model' to 'cheapest agent that finishes the job.'

Would you let it drive your laptop?
hits.video_tip: Screen-record a cursor moving on its own across a browser, a spreadsheet and an email draft, with a price tag overlay '$1 / $5 per 1M tokens' and a '9x cheaper per task (OpenAI claim)' badge. 20s, vertical. First-2s hook: 'This AI uses your computer for $1'.

hits.name: Claude
hits.hook: More than 25,000 nonprofits now use Claude. Most are small, local teams. We’re expanding Claude for Nonprofits with a plugin built with around 30 of them, adding skills for fundraising, marketing, and hiring grounded in
hits.draft_en:
AI agents did three very different real jobs this week:

1. Theo plugged a mic into his 'horrible' Sonos speakers and told Claude 'fix the sound.' It did.
2. Anthropic says 25,000+ nonprofits now use Claude, and it's adding a plugin with skills for fundraising, marketing and hiring.
3. Cursor shipped an Agent SDK: prompts in Markdown, tools in TypeScript, deploy anywhere.

Agents aren't a demo anymore. They're quietly becoming the default way to get small jobs done.

What's the first boring task you'd hand off?
